title: Sediqullah Atal: Afghanistan Milestones and Understanding a Batting Innings
excerpt: Explore Sediqullah Atal’s dated Harare century and Afghanistan career context. Learn strike rate, partnerships, boundaries and batting averages.
content:
Sediqullah Atal is an Afghanistan batter whose development offers a useful way to study an innings beyond its final total. His maiden ODI century against Zimbabwe in Harare in December 2024 is an established milestone. The official Afghanistan Cricket Board interview and the match scorecard give that achievement a date and format, which should remain attached when an older performance returns to search trends.

This guide explains the milestone and teaches readers how to interpret balls faced, partnerships and scoring rates. It is a career and cricket-learning article, not a live score for a later Afghanistan-Zimbabwe match. Fictional examples are labelled separately from the historical score, and no current selection or fitness claim is inferred from the older result.

## Who is Sediqullah Atal?

Sediqullah Atal is a professional cricketer associated with Afghanistan. ICC's player record lists his participation across identified competitions, while the Afghanistan Cricket Board documents his December 2024 maiden ODI hundred. A player record can contain several formats and representative levels. Those entries should not be merged into one unlabelled average or treated as proof that every listed event belongs to the same team category.

### A senior innings needs its format

An ODI, a T20 match and a youth or development-team appearance have different competition contexts. A score in one should not be inserted into another format's record. When collecting an innings, store team, opposition, date and format together. The number of runs alone cannot explain whether it was a short-format attack, a longer innings or a performance at another level.

### A name trend does not establish a new score

A player can trend because of a new match, a selection discussion or an old highlight. The trend list is not a scorecard. This article uses a clearly dated historical milestone and does not turn it into a claim about a match played in November 2026. A current match report needs its own fixture and verified result.

## What happened in Harare in December 2024?

Atal made 104 from 128 balls in Afghanistan's second ODI against Zimbabwe on 19 December 2024. The scorecard records Afghanistan at 286 for six and Zimbabwe at 54, producing a 232-run win. The board's interview identifies his maiden century and player-of-the-match performance. These facts belong to that game, not every later meeting between the teams.

### A personal hundred and a team win differ

The century is an individual batting milestone, while the winning margin is a team result. Bowling and other batting contributions also shaped the outcome. A clear report can recognise Atal's innings without claiming that one player alone produced the entire victory. Keeping the categories distinct also prevents a team score from being mistaken for an individual's runs.

### The innings score is not the winning margin

Afghanistan's total and the 232-run margin describe different quantities. The margin follows from the completed match comparison, not from the number of runs a single batter scored. A student should identify which score belongs to which team and whether the match was won by runs or wickets before attempting arithmetic or writing a summary.

## What does 104 from 128 balls tell you?

It gives the batter's runs and balls faced in that innings. Dividing runs by balls and multiplying by one hundred gives a strike rate of 81.25. The calculation describes scoring pace per hundred balls; it does not mean Atal faced one hundred balls or that the rate remained constant throughout the innings. Different phases can contribute to the same final average rate.

### An innings has a sequence

A batter might begin carefully, accelerate later or respond to wickets at the other end. A final strike rate does not reveal those phases by itself. To explain the sequence, use ball-by-ball records or reliable match reporting. Avoid inventing a story about slow starts or late hitting solely because the final rate seems to fit a familiar pattern.

### Balls faced are not the team's legal deliveries

The team innings includes balls faced by other batters and can include extras. A player's balls faced should not be used as the whole innings length. Store the categories separately when building a score table. The same care is needed with overs notation, where the digits after the point represent balls rather than a decimal fraction of an over.

## How do partnerships work?

A partnership concerns runs added while a particular pair is together, under the scorecard's definition. It is not always the sum of both batters' complete innings totals. One batter can score before a partner arrives or continue after the partnership ends. Extras can also affect the team's partnership total. Use the actual interval rather than an attractive but incorrect addition.

### Work through an original example

Imagine a fictional batter scores ten before a new partner arrives and later finishes with seventy. The new partner makes forty during their stand. Adding the full seventy and forty would include runs outside that partnership. The correct calculation needs the team score at the start and end of the stand, with the relevant scoring record.

### A large stand is a shared achievement

Partners can contribute through scoring, strike rotation and keeping the innings stable. Their roles need not be identical. A batter facing fewer balls can still support the stand, but the exact contribution should be described from evidence. Do not automatically assign a fixed role such as aggressor or anchor without examining the actual phase being discussed.

## How should a reader assess batting pace?

The required task depends on format, conditions, wickets and the state of the match. A rate that suits one situation may not suit another. Comparing innings fairly requires those labels. A faster rate is not automatically a better performance if it came from a tiny sample or a very different task. A slower rate is not automatically poor simply because another match produced more boundaries.

### A short sample moves sharply

A fictional batter hitting twelve from four balls has a strike rate of 300. That is a correct description of four balls, not proof of what would happen over a full innings. Display the runs and balls together. The rate becomes easier to interpret when the reader can see how little or how much evidence produced it.

### Format comparisons need restraint

ODI and T20 innings involve different lengths and tactical demands. A score achieved in one should not be judged solely against the typical pace of the other. The purpose is to understand the actual task, not find the largest available percentage. A fair report states the format before discussing whether the innings helped the team.

![Cricket equipment at Walker Cricket Ground in London in 2019; illustrative batting context, not Atal’s personal kit.](/images/editorial/trending-pk-20261107-daily/sediqullah-atal-inline.webp)

*Cricket equipment at Walker Cricket Ground in London in 2019; illustrative batting context, not Atal’s personal kit.*

## What can boundary numbers reveal?

Fours and sixes show one route by which runs were scored, but singles, twos and other scoring events also matter. A batter's total cannot be reconstructed from boundary counts alone unless the remaining runs are accounted for. The boundary contribution is a useful calculation when its inputs are clearly labelled and its limits remain visible.

### Use a fictional boundary calculation

Suppose a made-up innings contains six fours and two sixes. Those boundaries contribute thirty-six runs. If the innings total is sixty, the remaining twenty-four came through other scoring outcomes. These are teaching inputs, not an additional claim about Atal's Harare innings. The exercise shows how a total can contain both visible highlights and quieter accumulation.

### A boundary percentage is not an ability rating

A high share of boundary runs describes how that sample was built. It does not automatically measure technique, temperament or future potential. Conditions and field placement affect opportunities. Use the calculation to ask better questions about the innings rather than convert it into a permanent label attached to the player.

## How should an innings average be read?

Batting average uses runs and dismissals, while strike rate uses runs and balls. The two measures answer different questions. A not-out innings affects the dismissal count differently from an innings ending in dismissal. Do not divide runs by appearances and call the result an official batting average without checking the definition and the source's scope.

### A simple average example

Imagine a fictional player scores 180 runs across four innings and is dismissed three times. The batting average for that defined sample is sixty. Dividing by four would produce forty-five, which is runs per innings under that calculation, not the same batting-average measure. The example demonstrates why the denominator must match the label before a chart is created.

### An undefined value is not infinite talent

If a small sample contains no dismissals, the ordinary calculation cannot use a positive dismissal denominator. A dataset may display a special notation rather than a normal number. Preserve the convention and sample size. Do not turn the absence of a conventional average into a claim that the player is statistically unbeatable.

## What should historical photographs show?

A venue photograph can help identify where a milestone occurred, but it is not a portrait of Atal or proof that the pictured scene is the match. Use a caption that states the actual setting and date where available. Search results with a similar name should be rejected if the person cannot be identified reliably. A relevant illustrative image is better than a false player portrait.

### A career profile is not a selection announcement

An older appearance does not guarantee a place in the current squad. Team selection and availability need current official records. This guide uses historical performance evidence and does not infer today's lineup. The distinction matters when an article remains useful after several series have passed and the player is being discussed in a new context.

## A batting-analysis project for students

Create a table with innings date, format, runs, balls, dismissal status and source. Add formulas for strike rate and a separately defined average. Keep team totals outside the individual row unless clearly labelled. The exercise should produce a transparent summary rather than an unexplained overall score that mixes incompatible categories into one number.

### Add checks that protect meaning

Reject negative runs or balls, handle an empty ball sample without division by zero and keep not-out status explicit. Do not require every real innings to contain a boundary. A useful check guards an actual definition rather than imposing an invented rule merely to make the table look tidy. Preserve the original score notation alongside any parsed values.

### Connect cricket with study skills

The [class resources](/classes/) support the arithmetic, and the [programming courses](/courses/) can help students build a small scorecard calculator. Begin with fictional data, then add verified historical records with dates and sources. Keep the example calculations distinct from real performances. A good tool makes it easier to understand the innings without pretending to replace the official scorecard.

### Keep extras separate in a batting table

A team can receive runs through extras that do not belong to the batter’s personal total. When a partnership figure includes team scoring during the stand, that is another reason not to reconstruct it only from the two final innings totals. Store team extras and individual runs in separate columns. If the source does not show the partnership interval clearly, leave that calculation unavailable rather than force the numbers to agree. A neat total is not a substitute for the correct scoring definition.

## Questions about Sediqullah Atal

### Is the Harare century a November 2026 match result?

No. The innings discussed here belongs to 19 December 2024. It is used as a verified career milestone. A later match between Afghanistan and Zimbabwe requires its own record and should not inherit an older score simply because the player and opponents are familiar. The event date is part of the fact, not an optional decoration.

### Does a century explain an entire team victory?

It can be an important contribution, but the team result also involves other batting, bowling and fielding actions. A fair account identifies the individual milestone and the full match outcome separately. That gives the reader a more accurate picture than treating one score as though it alone established every part of the winning margin.
